issues.title: Eliminate intermittent held frames at clip loops in twelve-slot Perform playback
issues.description:
Remaining follow-up requested by Gordo on October 22 while publishing today's completed work through PR #51.

Observed on the native Tauri/WebView2 0.2.13 candidate, source commit 0150c43, public twelve-slot Redline Perform workflow, RANDOM, 1BT. Perform LIVE still tracks section/bank recall; Arrange UI is unmounted and Timing remains inactive with zero pending uploads.

Evidence:

* Ten-minute default-feature run passed existing 150 ms ordinary / 250 ms ramp source-cadence limits, 19 clip replacements per slot. Ordinary maximum 133.4 ms. Decoder drops remain nonzero.
* An earlier isolated 120-second repeat failed with simultaneous ordinary-source gaps up to 216.7 ms, away from a bank handoff.
* A later 120-second run spanning a user change from swing to dotted failed with 183.3 ms / 166.7 ms ordinary gaps at song 14.56–14.58 s, both presenting media time 0.041667: clip-loop boundary evidence, not proof dotted caused it.
* A separate 60-second dotted-only repeat passed; actual PGM cuts averaged 0.7204 s at 125 BPM, matching the expected 1.5-beat dotted cadence. No zero-drop claim.
* Ten-minute targeted trace: maximum synchronous renderAll 3.8 ms and video copy 2.4 ms; no long tasks or focus loss observed. All recorded seeks targeted near zero. These are API-call durations, not GPU execution timings.
* Baseline/immediates/shared-bindings/both two-minute comparisons all passed once; no reliable feature speed ranking or reason to revert either is established.

To do:

* Reproduce and correlate remaining ordinary held frames with HTMLVideo loop reset, decoding and presentation; distinguish intended STUTTER holds and slow SpeedRamp cadence.
* Evaluate reuse of existing GPU-resident frame banks or controlled loop prewarming to eliminate the decoder loop seek. Bound shared VRAM, deduplicate identical sources, preserve original quality and timeline semantics, and avoid duplicate workspace processing.
* Compare straight/swing/dotted and LINEAR/RANDOM under the same media and settings. Record actual PGM selections, bank swaps, drops and leading/trailing source gaps.
* Verify native signed release and public Chrome app. Keep rendering GPU/WGSL only; no CPU pixel renderer.
* Retain failing evidence and do not call this fixed from a single passing run or by loosening thresholds.

Evidence is under docs/qa/desktop-2026-10-22/ on PR #51; current ignored raw traces can be regenerated with svelte/scripts/verify-desktop-playback.ts.

Live tempo-change probe after this issue was created: the UI initially showed 1.2× / 150 BPM, key G and pitch +3, but the 60-second run included further user tempo changes (ordinary decoder playbackRate reached 1.3). It recorded 104 automatic PGM selections, Timing inactive/zero pending, and failed cadence with ordinary gaps up to 366.8 ms around song second 172.9, some mid-clip seeking. SpeedRamp reached 266.8 ms. This is a live-control stress sample, not a controlled fixed-1.2× comparison, and shows the remaining issue is not limited to clip-loop first frames. Raw report: output/native-tempo-1p2-60s.json in the working checkout. Correlate tempo-change resynchronization with these seeks before assigning causality.

Release checkpoint, October 22: PR #51 merged to main as 6d1e32f0c9db3e064f3552e4abc817c5c2b0291c after branch CI passed. Exact-main production deployment 39837942121 passed; public /health matches that SHA. Anonymous demo-media verification passed (14 files, 93,389,163 bytes, byte ranges); public browser loaded all twelve slots and GPU sampler ready. README screenshot verified rendered on GitHub at 2880×1772. Desktop v0.2.13 installers and updater manifest are published; updater download was fetched anonymously and its SHA-256 matched the GitHub asset digest. User will perform the installed-app update; do not claim the installed copy is updated yet. Remaining playback investigation stays Todo.

Completed on branch `codex/timing-layout-linear-tasks` in commit `3d7c43a`.

* Perform loop cadence: 60s Swing/linear + 60s Dotted/random, four decoder loops per ordinary slot, pass.
* Timing MIDI pressure: 60s Swing/balanced + 60s Dotted/random, pass.

issues.title: Timing tab: energy-ranked DENSITY + "by energy" repeats; PGM follows only fired triggers (port from Frame Lab)
issues.description:
## Scope: TIMING tab only

Change only the Timing workspace (`viewMode === 'timing'`): `svelte/src/lib/runtime/timing/triggers.ts` (`buildTimingSchedule`, `TimingTriggerConfig`) and the Timing panel UI.

**Do not touch** rack/Arrange DENSITY (`stores/midiTrigger.ts` `noteFires` / `firingTimes`, `MidiTimeline`, `MediaPatchBay`, `ArrangeView`). It stays as it is.

## Rule to port (proven in Frame Lab <issue id="4c9cb322-61e5-46fb-aa06-fd60a83e0d4f" label="V1S-210" href="https://linear.app/v1su4/issue/V1S-210/musicality-density-by-energy-dynamic-repeats-hit234ratchet-drums-fft" />, `web/src/benchmark/schedule.ts`)

1. **Energy score per trigger.**
   * MIDI notes: `velocity/127 × (0.25 + 0.75 × stem RMS envelope at the note-on)`. Read the envelope as the peak over the next 100 ms (`envelopeAt`).
   * Analyzed onsets: their existing flux strength.
2. **DENSITY 10–100% (new Timing control).** Per channel, keep only the loudest `density` share of triggers, so the quietest go first (`densityFloor`). This is deterministic: the same notes survive every pass, with no random draw. It replaces `stutterChance` as the musical thinning control. `threshold` can stay as a hard floor.
3. **Breathing.** After each burst, block new triggers for an extra `(1 − density) × 2` beats so the clip plays through.
4. **Repeats: FIXED | BY ENERGY.** "By energy" picks the burst shape from the trigger's energy rank within its channel (`energyRank`, `burstShape`):

   | Rank | Shape |
   | -- | -- |
   | < 35% | single hit |
   | < 65% | double |
   | < 85% | triplet (0, ⅔, 4⁄3 steps) |
   | < 95% | quad |
   | top 5% | ratchet (0, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.25, 2.5 steps) |

   Drop any repeat closer than 1/30 s to the previous one. FIXED keeps today's `StutterConfig.repeats`.
5. **PGM follows fired triggers only.** Wherever PGM switching is driven by trigger times in Timing, use the times of bursts that actually fired (after density and gap), not the raw trigger list. In Frame Lab, raw triggers made the program view ignore density: 623 switches at every density, against 416 / 210 / 136 / 47 at 100 / 70 / 40 / 10% after the fix.
6. **No effect interrupts another (hold until free).** Within a clip, a trigger that arrives while a burst or ramp is still running is dropped, not queued. On PGM, switch only to the deck whose burst is *starting*, and only after the on-screen burst has ended. A burst ends one repeat-interval after its last repeat, at a ramp's return to 1×, or half a beat after a single hit. Port `programTimeline` from Frame Lab `schedule.ts`. Also pin each burst's first cut to the exact trigger time, because beat round-trips are not bit-exact and an off-by-a-hair cut is not recognized as a burst start. In Frame Lab (8 decks, 70% density, by energy), PGM cuts landing mid-effect went from 24 to 0. **Tie-break:** clips that share a trigger channel start bursts at the same instant, so give PGM to the one shown longest ago. Lowest-index-wins starved 5 of 8 decks in Frame Lab: per-deck airtime went from 50/66/22/0/0/0/0/0 to 17/22/11/17/22/11/16/22.

## Acceptance

* The Timing panel has DENSITY and REPEATS controls, saved in timing settings and covered by undo.
* At 40% density the quietest 60% of triggers never fire, and the result is identical on every pass.
* PGM switch count drops with density.
* No PGM switch lands inside a running burst (unit test like Frame Lab's `program view waits for the on-screen burst…`).
* Unit tests cover `densityFloor`, `burstShape` and PGM switch times. Port the Frame Lab test "density keeps the loudest triggers…".
* Rack/Arrange density behaviour is unchanged.

MIDI/onset sources drive accepted-burst PGM switching, while the upper RAND/interval/feel controls are disabled and neutral; the left source indicators still follow the live clip. MIDI choices come from imported channels (saved bundle: vocals, synth, bass). Found the saved MIDI beat grid had been replaced by API rhythm data; retained the benchmarked MIDI grid and API section timestamps separately. Browser caught a missing PGM texture and loss of nine clip assignments during live editing; black-frame diagnosis is still open.

Burst starts follow the chosen MIDI note/onset source, with beat-relative subdivisions and energy-ranked hit/double/triplet/quad/ratchet shapes. This does not add a live FFT source or require a new onset for every repeat inside a burst. Default and persistence regression tests pass; full unit suite 824 passed, 8 skipped. Browser verified fresh Timing default shows BY ENERGY.Additional user-approved Timing refinements: Fixed/Random ramp cycle mode with four selectable musical lengths, seeded deterministically per trigger; no-interruption/busy-gap rules remain. Defaults for random choices: 1 beat, 2 beats, 1 bar, 2 bars. Random cycle replay and invalid persisted choices regression tests pass. Recorded at svelte/.artifacts/linear-acceptance/tempo-pitch-screen-recording.mp4. Full REC/PLAY/export acceptance still pending.

issues.title: Hand cuts during a take: quantized landing resets RAND's timer
issues.description:
Deck switches come from RAND (at its quantize: 1BT…8BR, STR8/SWNG/DOT) or from hand cuts (keys 0–9 / ARRANGE pads). A hand cut blinks until the next boundary, lands, and resets RAND's interval from that point; RAND stays on. Both are written into the take. Verify and cover with a test.

MIDI stress-test finding: the compiled PGM scheduler immediately reclaimed the previous automatic cut after a queued hand cut landed. Added priority for the landed manual choice for one complete bar; only a new accepted MIDI burst after that hold may resume automatic switching. Regression reproduced the override before the fix and now passes. The user observed the numeric keys queuing, landing, and holding successfully in @browser. Traditional beat/RAND cuts still restart their configured interval.

issues.description:
A take records everything needed to replay it exactly: which deck is on air over time, plus every deck's TIMING settings (RAMP/STUTTER, trigger source, EVERY, chances, curve, seed).

* Deck settings can't change during REC or PLAY.
* Snapshots are per section: each section plays back with the settings (and clip set) of its last take. Multiple snapshots per arrangement.
* Approach: store a settings snapshot + seed and re-run TIMING on playback; first add a determinism test (same settings + seed + song position ⇒ same output). If TIMING isn't repeatable, record effect events instead.

issues.title: Rack layout: previews always 16:9 and equal, PGM always dominant, consistent card controls
issues.description:
## Problem

On a short window, PR #28's per-card rule shrinks each rack preview to the height left in its own card. Cards carry different controls, so previews come out different sizes with side bars, and can rival the program monitor. Timing previews have borders they shouldn't.

## Fix

1. **Previews never squeeze:** full card width at 16:9, all ten the same size, no side bars.
2. **Minimum size, then scroll:** below the minimum the rack keeps its real size and the page scrolls. No squishing, no shrinking buttons. (Assumed scroll over the #28 zoom-to-fit; Gordo can flip it.)
3. **PGM monitor is always clearly bigger** than the rack previews, at every window size.
4. **Dense cards compressed:** Inception (bottom row) and Transition (top row) control sets fit without taking extra full rows, so cards in a row stay the same height.
5. **MIX strip aligned:** the vertical MIX label/knob row sits at the same left inset as the other vertical section labels (PACK / FIRE / SHPE…) on every card, top and bottom rows alike.
6. **Timing:** no borders on preview cards; same no-squeeze rule.

## Acceptance

* At tall, default and short windows: all previews identical size, 16:9, filling their cards; PGM larger than any preview; bottom row reachable.
* Every card's MIX row and section labels line up at the same left edge.

issues.title: PGM manual cuts quantize to the next bar + draw the queued cut ahead
issues.description:
## Goal

Ableton-style **launch quantize** for manual PGM changes.

* A manual PGM SOURCE change (the blinking "queued" state) always lands on the **next bar line** (4 beats), independent of the RAND/LINEAR cadence interval (1BT…8BR). Today one `intervalBeats` setting drives both, so a fast random cadence also makes manual cuts snap to single beats.
* Because the landing point is known in advance, the ARRANGE lanes **draw the queued cut ahead** at that bar (a ghost mark) until it fires — "drawing ahead of time" that still respects live changes.

## Acceptance

* Queue a source mid-bar → it fires on the next downbeat, whatever the cadence interval is.
* The ghost mark shows on the target slot's lane at that bar while queued, and disappears when it fires or is cancelled.
* RAND/LINEAR cadence still uses the interval buttons.

issues.title: Arrangement transport modes: LIVE / PLAY / REC (Ableton model)
issues.description:
## Goal

Make the arrangement's transport behave like Ableton's Session vs Arrangement split. Ableton is the reference: when there's a question about how it should behave, do what Ableton does.

## Modes (one explicit 3-way selector in ARRANGE, replacing the ARMED/OFF + REC toggles)

* **LIVE** (Ableton Session): play around. Manual PGM cuts only; the arrangement doesn't drive anything and nothing is recorded.
* **PLAY** (Ableton Arrangement playback): the timeline drives PGM cuts (today's ARMED).
  * A manual cut during PLAY **overrides** the arrangement, like launching a Session clip in Ableton. A **BACK TO ARRANGEMENT** button lights up; pressing it hands control back to the timeline at the playhead.
* **REC** (Ableton Arrangement Record): manual cuts are written **straight into the timeline** while transport runs. No separate COMMIT step.
  * Overdub vs replace, like Ableton punch/overdub. Replace clears cuts under the playhead while recording.

## Builds on

* <issue id="2605c675-9679-4e40-bcbf-129edbb67330" label="V1S-67" href="https://linear.app/v1su4/issue/V1S-67/arrangement-record-perform-section-loop-split-pane-ux" />: REC clips, COMMIT TAKE, OVERDUB (PR #30). This replaces the two-step record + commit with direct writing.
* <issue id="874e1f83-1f41-4498-be33-33c4f2f97e97" label="V1S-68" href="https://linear.app/v1su4/issue/V1S-68/arrangement-authoring-polish-no-midi-path" />: position-based section tracking (PR #30).

## Acceptance

* Mode selector visible in ARRANGE (and reflected in PERFORM).
* PLAY + manual cut → arrangement stops driving PGM, BACK TO ARRANGEMENT lights; pressing it resumes from the playhead.
* REC writes cuts live; stopping leaves them on the lanes as normal cuts.
* LIVE never changes the arrangement.

issues.title: SPEC: show output — projection mapping + footage-driven live lighting (Art-Net/sACN), on one beat clock
issues.description:
> **Moved 2026-10-07** from Frame Lab to *Beatsmaxxer Pro Experimental (Desktop)*. Work happens on `beatsmaxxer-pro` branch `experimental/desktop`, desktop (Tauri) only. Frame Lab stays a benchmark; it only measures cost (decks held with N outputs / M universes).

## Vision (from the user)

The tool is footage-first: many video clips cut live to music. That output is then **mapped onto screens, stages and objects**, including projection, while **live lighting** (racks, trusses, fixtures) runs from the same show. It should work alongside existing lighting setups or standalone, for example projection-only.

This is not the Notch, TouchDesigner or Sentinel category of generative shaders and AI visuals. The closest references are:

* **Resolume Arena**: output mapping plus DMX/Art-Net output.
* **MadMapper**: projection mapping plus LED/DMX pixel mapping.
* **Millumin**: timeline shows with mapping and DMX cues.
* **disguise**: the high end.
* Open source: **Splash** (multi-projector mapping and blending) and **QLC+ / OLA** (lighting control).

## Design reference: Sentinel workspace (public)

Source: [https://github.com/ood-labs/sentinel-workspace-public](<https://github.com/ood-labs/sentinel-workspace-public>). The app itself is closed source; this repo holds the agent workspace and example projects.

* **Bundles.** One connection carries a video texture plus named data channels (laser scan paths, fixture records, mattes) from the same frame. Looks switch through a Mux as whole bundles, so the projector, lasers and lights change together. Each channel has its own transition: video crossfades, data snaps at start, mid or end. Fixture data converts to DMX universes after the Mux. See `knowledge/bundle-links.md`.
* `projects/phage_stage`**.** A 196-fixture arena rig (beam movers, strobes, pixel bars on a kinetic truss) with:
  * banks of 16 looks: STATIC, EFFECTS, COLOR and FULL
  * energy tiers CALM, GROOVE, BUILD and CRAZY
  * TAP, SYNC and BPM transport, plus BLACKOUT and STROBE that act while held
  * a mouse desk or Ableton Push 2 as the controller
  * 64 Hz on a laptop RTX 5060. `docs/PROCESS.md` describes cutting GPU time from 41 ms to 5.8 ms.
* `projects/laser_mapping_lab`**.** Calibration with a 5×5 mesh against a projected grid, zoning masks, and a sync sweep that measures laser-to-projector latency.

**Takeaway: model each look as a bundle of footage decks, lighting cues and mapping data, switched atomically on the beat clock, with a transition rule for each channel.** Energy-tier banks and tap/BPM transport fit Frame Lab's trigger and groove system.

## How it builds on Frame Lab

1. **Mapping pass.** Every deck is already composited in WebGPU textures. Add output surfaces with a corner-pin or mesh-warp shader, soft-edge blending for multiple projectors, and masks. The GPU cost is negligible next to decode.
2. **Pixel mapping to lighting.** Define fixtures (position on the canvas, channel layout, universe). Sample the composited frame on the GPU each frame, read back a small buffer, and send it as **Art-Net or sACN**.
3. **One clock.** The beat and trigger schedule that cuts the video also fires lighting cues (chases, strobes, colour hits), with the same groove options (straight, swing, dotted).
4. **Platform.** Browsers can't send raw UDP, so Art-Net/sACN, Spout/Syphon/NDI and multi-window projector output live on the **Tauri Rust side** (<issue id="195908e8-983d-423d-94e7-14b1673280b1" label="V1S-204" href="https://linear.app/v1su4/issue/V1S-204/desktop-track-tauri-native-playback-angle-wgpu-native-decode-hap" />). The web build can preview mapping and lighting, or use a WebSocket bridge.

## Measure with Frame Lab

* How many decks still hold on-time cuts with N mapped outputs and M lighting universes enabled.
* Trigger-to-light latency compared with trigger-to-pixel latency.

## Open questions for the user

* Which fixtures and protocols are in the rigs you use (Art-Net, sACN, DMX over USB like Enttec)?
* Do you need to interoperate with an existing lighting console (grandMA, Chamsys) as a slave or master, or run standalone?
